title: 高市首相VS．野党党首の党首討論　今国会での開催の行方は　細切れで議論深まらぬ指摘も
extracted_text: 連休明け以降の後半国会では、高市早苗首相（自民党総裁）と野党党首が1対1で論戦を交わす党首討論が実現するかが注目される。野党は与党に開催を繰り返し求めているものの、今国会で実現には至っていない。過去には首相が衆院解散を明言するなどの名場面が生まれたが、討論時間の短さから不要論にもさらされてきた。開催方式も焦点になりそうだ。 党首討論は平成12年、英国議会の「クエスチョンタイム（QT）」を参考に正式導入された。他の審議と異なり、首相が質問に答えるだけでなく逆質問や反論もできるのが特徴だ。民主党政権下の24年11月には野田佳彦首相（当時）が自民の安倍晋三総裁（同）との討論で、衆院定数削減と引き換えに衆院解散を明言する見せ場もあった。
translated_text: In the latter half of the Diet session after the consecutive holidays, attention is focused on whether a party leader debate, where Prime Minister Sanae Takashi (LDP President) directly confronts opposition party leaders one-on-one, will be realized. The opposition has repeatedly requested the ruling party to hold such a debate, but it has yet to materialize in this Diet session. In the past, dramatic moments have occurred, such as when the prime minister explicitly stated the dissolution of the Lower House, but the debates have also faced criticism due to their short duration. The format of the debate is also expected to become a point of contention. The party leader debate was formally introduced in 2000, modeled after the British Parliament's "Question Time (QT)". Unlike other deliberations, its distinguishing feature is that not only does the prime minister answer questions, but they can also pose reverse questions and counterarguments. In November 2012 during the Democratic Party of Japan administration, then-Prime Minister Yoshihiko Noda faced LDP President Shinzo Abe in a debate, creating a notable moment where he explicitly mentioned dissolving the Lower House in exchange for reducing its seat count.
title_en: Party Leader Debate: PM Takashi vs. Opposition Leaders - Will It Be Held This Diet Session? Critics Note Fragmented Discussions Lacking Depth
